title: Ordinary and locally adaptive IBM smoothing
text: Ordinary IBM uses one diffusion standard deviation τ\tau, λj=τ2\lambda_j=\tau^2. smoothing_prior accepts valid Stan code involving positive parameter tau. tau constrained positive, symmetric Stan distributions examples induce corresponding truncated (half) distributions. Priors specified internally standardized response time scale.
code: fit_lognormal <- ibm(t, y)  fit_half_normal <- ibm(   t, y,   smoothing_prior = "tau ~ normal(0, 0.5);" )  fit_half_t <- ibm(   t, y,   smoothing_prior = "tau ~ student_t(3, 0, 0.5);" )

title: Ordinary and locally adaptive IBM smoothing
text: Observations conditionally independent given function. family argument provides Gaussian, Student-t, Bernoulli, binomial, Poisson, negative-binomial, lognormal, gamma, beta, exponential likelihoods. Binomial models use trials; Poisson negative-binomial models optionally use exposure. Gaussian Student-t responses standardized. families IBM function latent predictor: logit scale Bernoulli, binomial, beta means; log-mean scale Poisson, negative-binomial, gamma, exponential observations; mean-log scale lognormal observations. Priors phi negative-binomial, gamma, beta likelihoods controlled log_phi. complete generated Stan program can returned, printed, saved without supplying observations:
code: fit_poisson <- ibm(   t, counts, family = "poisson", exposure = person_time,   adaptive = TRUE )  fit_binomial <- ibm(   t, events, family = "binomial", trials = sample_sizes,   adaptive = TRUE ) code <- ibm(family = "poisson", adaptive = TRUE, get_code = TRUE) ibm(family = "poisson", adaptive = TRUE, print_code = TRUE) ibm(family = "poisson", adaptive = TRUE,     stan_file = "ibm_poisson.stan")

title: Ordinary and locally adaptive IBM smoothing
text: adaptive model uses λj=γξj,ξj∼C+(0,1),γ∼C+(0,sγ). \sqrt{\lambda_j}=\gamma\xi_j,\qquad \xi_j\sim C^+(0,1),\qquad \gamma\sim C^+(0,s_\gamma). intervals can strongly regularized heavy-tailed local scales allow selected intervals substantially larger derivative innovations. derivative remains continuous Brownian path; local scale controls much slope permitted evolve interval. Internally, locations mapped [0,1][0,1]. Gaussian Student-t responses standardized; families use latent predictor scale. local scales set one, stochastic departure initial linear trajectory standard deviation t3/2/31/2t^{3/2}/3^{1/2}, whose maximum 1/31/21/3^{1/2}. arguments global_upper = U global_alpha = alpha therefore calibrate selected half-Cauchy half-normal prior Pr⁡{γ/3>U}=α. \Pr\{\gamma/\sqrt{3}>U\}=\alpha. calibration independent number placement state locations. Posterior samples function derivative available directly:
code: fit_adaptive <- ibm(   t, y,   adaptive = TRUE,   global_prior = "half_cauchy",   global_upper = 1,   global_alpha = 0.05,   chains = 4,   iter = 2000,   adapt_delta = 0.99 )  # Same model in centered HMC coordinates fit_adaptive_centered <- ibm(   t, y,   adaptive = TRUE,   parameterization = "centered",   global_prior = "half_normal",   global_upper = 1,   global_alpha = 0.05,   chains = 4,   iter = 2000,   adapt_delta = 0.99 )  fit_adaptive_regularized <- ibm(   t, y,   adaptive = TRUE,   adaptive_prior = "regularized_horseshoe",   slab_scale = 1,   slab_df = 4,   chains = 4,   iter = 2000,   adapt_delta = 0.99 )  plot(fit_adaptive) plot_diffusion(fit_adaptive) summary(fit_adaptive) f_draws <- get_samples(fit_adaptive, "f") derivative_draws <- get_samples(fit_adaptive, "fprime") lambda_draws <- get_samples(fit_adaptive, "lambda_interval")

title: Integrated Brownian Motion Smoothing
text: ibmsmooth fits integrated Brownian motion smoothers conditionally independent observations using Stan. package contains two latent models: ordinary IBM one positive smoothing parameter user-supplied Stan prior parameter; locally adaptive IBM horseshoe global–local shrinkage derivative diffusion rate. locations (t_j<t_{j+1}), (j=t{j+1}-t_j), state (x_j=(f’(t_j),f(t_j))^T), models use exact transition [ x_{j+1}x_j,_j  N_2. ] Ordinary IBM sets (_j=^2). adaptive model sets (_j=2_j2), (_j^+(0,1)) reference-process-calibrated half-Cauchy half-normal prior (). mapping time ([0,1]), global_upper = U global_alpha = alpha set prior scale ({/>U}=). uses maximum reference-process standard deviation independent observation grid.

title: Integrated Brownian Motion Smoothing
code: library(ibmsmooth)  fit <- ibm(t, y)  # Any valid Stan prior statement involving the positive parameter `tau`. fit_half_t <- ibm(   t, y,   smoothing_prior = "tau ~ student_t(3, 0, 0.5);" )  fit_adaptive <- ibm(   t, y,   adaptive = TRUE,   global_prior = "half_cauchy",   global_upper = 1,   global_alpha = 0.05 )  # Centered implementation of the same model fit_adaptive_centered <- ibm(   t, y,   adaptive = TRUE,   parameterization = "centered",   global_prior = "half_normal",   global_upper = 1,   global_alpha = 0.05 )  # Optional finite-slab regularized horseshoe fit_adaptive_regularized <- ibm(   t, y,   adaptive = TRUE,   adaptive_prior = "regularized_horseshoe",   slab_scale = 1,   slab_df = 4 )  # The default regularized_retry = "ask" also detects the specific combination # of poor HMC diagnostics and local scales pinned near the half-Cauchy boundary. # In an interactive session it offers to run the regularized fit above.  plot(fit_adaptive) plot_diffusion(fit_adaptive)  # Visual model checks plot_pp_check(fit_adaptive) plot_pp_check(fit_adaptive, type = "density") plot_prior_posterior(fit_adaptive, seed = 123)  # Timing, ESS, R-hat, divergences, treedepth, acceptance, and E-BFMI diagnostics <- get_diagnostics(fit_adaptive) diagnostics$overview

title: Fit an integrated Brownian motion smoother — ibm
text:
Time mapped unit interval. Gaussian Student-t responses centered scaled unit standard deviation; families, f represented usual link scale (logit Bernoulli/binomial beta means; log mean count, gamma, exponential observations; mean-log lognormal observations). Locations infer_at evaluated fitting using exact conditional IBM bridges, avoiding additional Stan parameters. adaptive fit, unit-diffusion IBM departure initial linear trajectory standard deviation t^(3/2) / sqrt(3) standardized domain. maximum [0, 1] therefore grid-independent reference scale sigma_ref = 1 / sqrt(3). selected global prior assigned scale s_gamma Pr(gamma / sqrt(3) > global_upper) = global_alpha. fitted object retains sigma_ref s_gamma data$reference_sd fit_spec$global_scale. non-centered parameterization represents state transition standard-normal innovations. usually better starting point observations sparse noisy, adaptive local scales strongly shrunk. centered parameterization samples f fprime directly transition density. can efficient latent states large local changes strongly identified likelihood. Neither parameterization dominates every dataset. Fit practical compare divergences, R-hat, effective sample size per second, leapfrog counts, treedepth hits get_diagnostics(). adaptive_prior = "regularized_horseshoe", effective local scale $$	ilde\xi_j^2 =  rac{c^2\xi_j^2}{c^2+\gamma^2\xi_j^2},$$ \(c = \code{slab_scale}\sqrt{c_{\mathrm{aux}}}\) \(c_{\mathrm{aux}}\sim\mathrm{InvGamma}(
u/2,
u/2)\) \(
u=\code{slab_df}\). Thus effective interval diffusion standard deviation \(\gamma	ilde\xi_j\) approaches finite slab scale extreme local scales. can stabilize isolated, strongly identified changes preserving horseshoe shrinkage near zero. adaptive transition interval length \(\Delta_j\) exactly bivariate normal mean \((f'_j, f_j+\Delta_j f'_j)\) covariance \(\gamma^2\xi_j^2 Q(\Delta_j)\), \(Q(\Delta)=((\Delta,\Delta^2/2),(\Delta^2/2,\Delta^3/3))\).
